- Cloud environments. Manage the environments that support prototyping features across our Android and web applications alongside changes to one or more of our backend microservices.

- API and event-driven architecture. Gatekeep the quality of our APIs, webhooks, and event-driven architecture in an open contributor model.

- Agentic enablement. Continually improve our internal agentic harnesses (skills, context, and tooling) that allow other engineers and less technical colleagues to develop and prototype on our platform.

- Agentic automation. Add agentic automation to all appropriate areas of the platform stack without compromising on quality.

Must Have 

- Distributed systems experience. You've designed or meaningfully contributed to distributed backend systems, and understand event-driven patterns, asynchronous messaging, and the trade-offs at scale.

- API design and evolution. You've designed APIs that other teams and clients depend on, and you understand the trade-offs between clean design, backwards compatibility, and speed.

- Database and schema fluency. Practical experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL or similar), including schema design, indexing, migrations, and query optimisation. Working knowledge of at least one non-relational store.

- Cloud infrastructure. Experience deploying and operating distributed services on AWS, GCP, or Azure.

- AI-native engineering. You've shipped production code with frontier AI tools (Cursor, Claude Code, or similar) and push further into agentic workflows rather than push back on them.

Nice to Have (or We Can Teach)

Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

🛠️ About our Robotaxi Teams 

The Robotaxi team is taking Wayve's AI Driver to its first public-scale deployment, with fare-paying riders on global ride-hail platforms. This team owns the end-to-end performance operating system for the product: the metrics, triage, and release gates that decide whether the autonomy is good enough to ship, and stays great release over release. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve's mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

- Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role 

We're hiring a Direct Tax Lead to own our US income tax provision, compliance, and controls, reporting to the Head of Tax. ElevenLabs operates through its US entity and ~9 international entities and is growing fast, which means the provision, the compliance calendar, and the controls around them need a dedicated owner.

This is a hands-on ownership role. The provision and returns are prepared by external providers; you manage those engagements and are accountable for the output. You'll own the quarterly and annual ASC 740 provision (deferreds, valuation allowance, uncertain tax positions, rate rec, footnote disclosures), the US federal and state compliance calendar (returns, extensions, estimated payments), and the technical work underneath it: §174 capitalization, §382 and NOL tracking.

You'll also assist in designing, documenting, and operating controls, and write the memos that support our positions, working directly with our Big 4 advisors and external auditors alongside the Head of Tax.

On our most strategic accounts, Deployment Strategists in our Forward Deployed Engineering team already build account-specific business cases and ROI narratives as part of delivery. You will partner with them rather than duplicate that work. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.

This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. We are looking for a builder and a doer: someone who can engage credibly with senior customer stakeholders, get deep into a customer's operations and data, build rigorous models themselves, and turn ambiguous business problems into clear, actionable recommendations.

You will define how ElevenLabs understands, measures, and communicates customer value globally.

- Shape value from the beginning. Partner with Revenue teams and prospects early in the sales cycle to understand customer priorities, identify high-value opportunities, and establish the business case for investing in ElevenLabs.

· Implémente ou étend la génération paresseuse d’explications pour les contraintes Sum, AllDifferent et d’autres contraintes globales

title: Alternant·e Growth Marketing Manager | Thiga Academy
description:
Alternance · Paris 9e · Télétravail · rythme d’alternance souhaité 3 semaines entreprise / 1 semaine école 

Thiga en 30 secondes : 

Thiga est un cabinet de conseil spécialisé en IA et en digital. Nous accompagnons les plus grands groupes et scale-ups françaises : Decathlon, Doctolib, AXA, ManoMano, Mirakl, Disney, Leboncoin et une centaine d'autres. Nous sommes 200, majoritairement à Paris.
Thiga Academy, c'est notre organisme de formation. On y forme les équipes produit (Product Managers, Product Owners, Designers, Product Leaders) et celles qui veulent le devenir : product management, product discovery, leadership produit, et IA appliquée au produit. En inter-entreprise comme en intra, on transmet ce que nos consultants pratiquent chez nos clients tous les jours

Pourquoi ce poste : 

L'Academy forme chaque année 2000 professionnels et son offre est solide. Le problème : aujourd'hui, elle ne communique presque pas. Peu de contenu, peu de présence, une notoriété très en dessous de ce que le catalogue mérite.

C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. On cherche quelqu'un pour construire, mesurer et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition de l'Academy à partir de zéro : quels canaux, quels messages, quel funnel, avec quels résultats. Pas pour décorer le catalogue, pour le remplir.

Ce que tu vas faire 🖇 

1. Construire et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition, avec le Head of Marketing & Events 

- 
Structurer le tunnel d'acquisition de bout en bout : quels canaux amènent du trafic, ce qui convertit en lead, ce qui déclenche l'inscription

- 
Tester des canaux et des formats en continu (LinkedIn organique et payant, email, SEO, partenariats, salons) et couper vite ce qui ne marche pas

- 
Créer et itérer les landing pages du catalogue et des sessions, pensées pour convertir dès le premier jet et retravaillées à partir de la donnée

- 
Mettre en place les séquences email dans HubSpot : nurturing, relances, réactivation des contacts dormants, avec un test A/B sur les objets et les CTA

- 
Accompagner le lancement des nouvelles formations avec un plan d'acquisition dédié, pas seulement un plan de com

- 
Créer les supports nécessaires au tunnel avec Figma (catalogue, plaquettes, brochures) en gardant en tête qu'un support existe pour convertir, pas pour exister

- 
Représenter l'Academy sur des salons et événements, avec un objectif de leads qualifiés en sortie, pas juste de présence

2. Mesurer, analyser, arbitrer 

Le nerf du poste. Sans mesure, pas de growth, juste du marketing qui se raconte des histoires.

- 
Suivre les KPIs qui comptent à chaque étape du tunnel : trafic, taux de clic, taux de conversion en lead, taux de conversion en inscrit, coût d'acquisition par inscrit, taux de remplissage des sessions

- 
Construire les dashboards HubSpot qui donnent une vision claire de ce qui marche, canal par canal, campagne par campagne

- 
Identifier où le tunnel fuit et proposer les hypothèses à tester pour colmater

- 
Faire remonter les résultats au Head of Marketing & Events pour arbitrer les prochains messages, offres et canaux, avec des chiffres, pas des impressions

3. Faire vivre la marque et la communauté qui nourrissent le funnel 

L'acquisition ne marche pas sans contenu ni preuve sociale. C'est le carburant du tunnel.

- 
Poser la ligne éditoriale et la faire vivre : posts LinkedIn, articles, newsletters, formats courts autour du product et de l'IA

- 
Animer la relation avec les alumni et la communauté d'apprenants : témoignages, cas concrets, un bouche-à-oreille qu'on peut transformer en canal d'acquisition mesurable

L'IA n'est pas une option chez nous , c'est la pierre angulaire de notre façon de travailler, et on attend de toi que tu aies cette fibre. Concrètement, tu t'appuieras sur l'IA à chaque étape : générer et itérer des variantes de copies avec Claude, produire des visuels avec Nano Banana et Figma, des teasers avec HeyGen, ou transformer une transcription Granola en article et en carrousel LinkedIn. C'est ce qui te permet d'avancer vite et de tester dix fois plus d'hypothèses qu'une équipe classique.

La stack que tu vas pratiquer 🧰 

Le growth marketing moderne, c'est une combinaison d'intuition testée par la donnée, de vitesse d'exécution et de bons outils au bon moment.

- 
LLM et agents : Claude (Pro et Code), Gemini

- 
Génération visuelle et audio : Nano Banana, Adobe Firefly, ElevenLabs, HeyGen

- 
Marketing ops : HubSpot (CRM, marketing hub, workflows), Luma, Phantom Buster

- 
Prise de notes et capitalisation : Granola, Notion AI

- 
Vibe coding (en bonus, pour les profils qui veulent aller plus loin) : Lovable, Cursor pour bricoler des micro-outils internes

Tu n'as pas besoin de tout maîtriser à l'arrivée. On attend une vraie curiosité et l'envie de pratiquer, pas un CV exhaustif.

Le profil que nous recherchons 🌟 

- 
Formation : école de commerce ou de communication, en M1 ou M2, idéalement avec une spécialisation marketing, growth ou entrepreneuriat

- 
Pratique IA personnelle prouvée : tu as un side project, un compte ChatGPT ou Claude que tu utilises tous les jours, un workflow Make ou n8n que tu as construit, un agent custom, un blog assisté par LLM, un repo GitHub, ou n'importe quoi qui démontre que l'IA est dans ta vie.

- 
Réflexe growth : tu penses en funnel avant de penser en campagne, tu formules des hypothèses avant de produire, et tester puis mesurer te vient plus naturellement que produire pour produire

- 
Appétence data : Excel ou Google Sheets n'ont pas de secret pour toi, et l'idée de creuser un dashboard pour comprendre pourquoi un taux de conversion a bougé t'intéresse plus qu'elle ne t'ennuie

- 
Fibre communication : tu sais écrire pour être lu, tu as déjà animé une page, un compte ou une communauté

- 
Rigueur opérationnelle et sens du détail : tu sais qu'une séquence email qui commence par « Bonjour {prénom} », ça fait tâche, et qu'un A/B test mal cadré ne prouve rien

- 
Sensibilité business : tu comprends les concepts MQL, CAC, NPS, et tu sais qu'une belle campagne ne vaut rien si elle ne remplit pas les sessions 

Au-delà des hard skills, on recherche surtout quelqu’un de curieux, volontaire, débrouillard et qui n’a pas peur de proposer des nouvelles idées !

Ce qu'on offre 🎊 

- 
Stack IA premium : Claude, Gemini, et accès facilité à tous les outils IA quand ils sont pertinents pour ton travail

- 
Encadrement et présence au quotidien de membres de l'équipe marketing pointus sur les sujets growth, événementiel et IA

- 
Cadence de suivi : 1-to-1 hebdomadaire avec le Head of Marketing & Events. Fonctionnement quotidien en équipe avec les autres Head of (Content, Design) et le CMO

- 
Cadre de travail : bureaux 23 rue Taitbout (Paris 9), équipe marketing de 8 personnes

- 
Rémunération : grille légale alternance, transparente dès l'entretien

Le process 🎢 
Envoie ton CV, un lien vers un side project ou portfolio (même bricolé). Pas de lettre de motivation.

En termes de déroulé, tu auras : 

- 
Un premier call avec notre Talent Acquisition Manager

- 
Un échange avec le Head of Marketing & Event 

- 
Un case study à préparer et présenter 

- 
Un dernier entretien avec Hugo, notre CEO

Thiga accueille toutes les personnes compétentes et passionnées et s'engage en faveur de la diversité culturelle, l'égalité de genre et l'emploi des travailleurs handicapés — au contraire nous considérons la diversité comme une grande richesse !

title: Senior Legal Counsel
description:
About AQEMIA 

AQEMIA is a drug invention company dedicated to creating entirely new medicines to address major unmet medical needs. At the core of our mission is QEMI , our proprietary molecule-invention platform, which uniquely combines cutting-edge science with advanced technology. Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles.

What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing never-before-seen molecules , without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies.

Our most advanced preclinical programs are currently in vivo optimization , targeting diseases still waiting for effective treatments, offering our teams the opportunity to work on science that can make a real difference in people’s lives.

For more information, visit AQEMIA.com, our WTTJ Page , and our LinkedIn . 

About our Team 

AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery.

This close collaboration across disciplines is central to our approach, enabling us to tackle complex scientific challenges from first principles and translate cutting-edge ideas into novel therapeutic candidates. At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention.

The role 

AQEMIA's drug discovery programs and AI platform increasingly create value through licensing deals and strategic partnerships with pharma and biotech companies.

As our first in-house Legal Counsel, you will lead the legal work on these deals from term sheet to signing. You'll make sure each licensing agreement maximises value creation for Aqemia, protects our IP, and the platform behind every program. Beyond licensing, you will become the trusted legal partner for CEO, founders, leadership and teams across the company, covering IP and patents, operational contracts, data and AI, compliance and corporate matters alongside specialist external counsel. Within a year, you will have shaped how legal works at AQEMIA: issues will be mapped and anticipated, processes will be practical, and leadership will rely on you for well-judged legal advice. Reporting to the Corporate Finance Manager, you’ll have a rare chance to sit at the centre of the deals that bring AI-discovered drug candidates to partners, and to grow well beyond licensing into a broad in-house role.

Responsibilities 

- Licensing & partnerships: lead the legal work on licensing and collaboration deals, drafting and negotiating agreements from term sheet to signing.

- Deal strategy: work with BD, Finance and Leadership to turn commercial goals into contract terms, while protecting AQEMIA's platform and other programs.

- IP & patents: support IP protection and patent-related decisions with scientific teams and external patent counsel.

- Operational contracts: draft and negotiate NDAs, MTAs, CRO, vendor, software and data agreements, including contractual questions on data use and AI.

- Corporate & compliance: adresss GDPR, regulatory, compliance and dispute-related matters with specialist support where needed, and support corporate and fundraising matters in coordination with Finance and external advisors.

- Legal processes: own templates and approval workflows, highlight key contract obligations and deadlines to relevant teams, and manage external counsel.

Qualifications 

- Law degree or equivalent professional legal qualification.

- 5+ years of legal experience , including time at a law firm in a life sciences practice. In-house experience at a biotech or pharma company is a strong plus.

- Licensing: hands-on experience drafting and negotiating biotech or pharma licensing agreements yourself, not only coordinating external counsel.

- Deal knowledge: strong understanding of licensing mechanics and IP ownership in drug discovery (scope, exclusivity, financials, termination).

- Communication: excellent English drafting and negotiation skills, and you can explain legal points clearly to non-lawyers.

- Mindset: autonomous, pragmatic and eager to learn legal topics beyond your current expertise.

Nice‑to‑Have 

- In-house experience at a biotech, pharma or TechBio company, ideally a startup or lean legal team.

- Exposure to AI, data or technology platform agreements (data rights, model training, ownership of outputs).

- Experience building legal processes, templates or contract management from scratch.

- Business development or commercial experience alongside your legal background.

- Professional French.

Our recruitment process

- 1 - Hiring Manager’s interview: you’ll meet directly with your future manager (45 mins)

- 2 - Technical assessment of your skills through a Business Case (60 mins)

- 3 - Cultural fit interview with our co-founder and COO Emmanuelle (45 mins)

- 4 - Final interview with our co-founder and CEO Maximilien (45 mins)

Why Join Us ? 

At AQEMIA, we work for a mission: joining us means having your own impact on changing the way drugs are discovered, and helping to shape the direction of our fast-growing company and team. 

Expanding Drug Discovery Pipeline : Focused on critical therapeutic areas like Oncology, CNS, Immuno-inflammation... with in vivo proof of concept/patent stage programs. Collaborations with top Pharma, including a $140M Sanofi deal.

title: Security Engineer (Hybrid or Remote)
description:

We’re an EMI-licensed fintech in a fully cloud-native AWS environment, we use AI heavily, and we’re growing fast. We need someone who can lead technical initiatives independently, influence our security architecture, challenge approaches that no longer fit, and explain it clearly to engineers and leadership.

Your Mission Detection & Response (SIEM) — our top priority - Own SIEM alerting end-to-end: ship logs from endpoints, IdP, VPN, SaaS, and cloud; write and tune detection rules; cut false positives.
- Act as first responder for security incidents — investigate, contain, drive to closure with clear runbooks — and feed recurring issues back into preventive controls.
Identity, Access & SaaS - Administer the IdP (SSO via SAML/OIDC, MFA, conditional access) and run access recertification end-to-end across IdP, SaaS, AWS, and internal tools — scope, evidence, follow-through on revocations.
- Hunt down over-permissive and stale access, enforce least privilege and PAM, catch SoD gaps, and make JML and third-party access work in practice.
- Improve SaaS security posture (Google/Microsoft, Slack, GitHub, others) and apply DLP controls to limit data leakage.
Endpoint, Email & Phishing Defense - Keep the endpoint stack healthy and well-tuned — MDM, XDR/AV, device-compliance checks for VPN/ZTNA — and define posture requirements (disk encryption, EDR present, OS version) with automated remediation.
- Defend against phishing and spoofing — secure email gateway rules, DMARC/SPF/DKIM — and run phishing simulations and security awareness, acting on the results.
Automation & Ownership - Build internal tooling and automate repetitive operations — reduce manual work, don't just operate it.
- Own the roadmap for your areas: identify gaps, lead initiatives independently, and raise the bar rather than just maintain it.

Your Profile - 5+ years in security operations, corporate/IT security, or endpoint engineering.
- Strong with a SIEM (Splunk, Elastic, Panther, Sumo Logic) — detection engineering and incident response — plus an identity provider (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace), access recertification, and least-privilege / PAM.
- Working knowledge of endpoint security (MDM, XDR/EDR/AV) and email / phishing defense.
- Practical experience securing how a company uses AI internally: shadow AI discovery, DLP for AI tools, controls for AI assistants and agents, and a working risk framework for adopting new ones. You've done this for real, not from a vendor pitch deck.
- Strong scripting and automation skills — you build tooling against APIs, not just configure consoles.

title: Project Security Officer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

Join us as a Project Security Officer, where you’ll be the primary security interface for the Nyx project, connecting Mission Operations with central security functions, engineering teams, suppliers, and external partners. You’ll translate requirements into practical, verifiable controls across our mission systems, working hands-on with engineers, technicians, and operators from concept through operations. Applications at all seniority levels are considered.

Key Responsibilities 

- Act as the single point of contact for security-related topics on the Nyx project.

- Translate company policies, customer requirements, regulations, and threat intelligence into project-specific security requirements, architectures, procedures, and verification criteria.

- Maintain the integrated project security risk picture across cyber, physical, personnel, supply-chain, export-control, and security-architecture domains.

- Flow security requirements into systems, subsystems, suppliers, and operations, and verify their implementation with objective evidence.

- Work hands-on with engineers and the security team to implement secure configurations, access controls, segmentation, monitoring, vulnerability remediation, encryption, and other cybersecurity controls.

- Support threat modelling, risk assessments, security-by-design, system reviews, supplier assessments, security readiness, and assurance activities throughout the project lifecycle.

What we would love to see from you: 

The ideal candidate will have:

- Bachelor’s degree in cybersecurity, computer science, engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 3+ years of relevant experience in cybersecurity engineering, systems security, infrastructure security, operational technology, embedded security, project security, or a related hands-on field.

- Experience working across multiple technical domains, such as networks, operating systems, applications, communications, embedded systems, hardware, or data centers.

- Experience translating security requirements, policies, regulations, or customer expectations into system designs, technical controls, configurations, tests, procedures, and objective evidence.

- Experience in security risk management, including risk-based vulnerability prioritization, threat and risk analysis, security testing, incident response, supplier and supply-chain security, and secure system integration.

- Practical experience configuring, hardening, troubleshooting, or monitoring real systems—not only reviewing designs or producing documentation.

- Ability to integrate cyber, physical, personnel, supply-chain, export-control, and security-architecture considerations into a coherent project-security approach.

- Strong communication, organization, project-management, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to build trust across Corporate IT, engineering, suppliers, central security functions, and Mission Operations.

Bonus qualifications:

- Experience working with operators in control rooms, mission-control environments, NOCs, SOCs, launch campaigns, test operations, or other time-critical operational settings.

- Experience securing spacecraft, launch systems, ground stations, mission-control centers, satellite communications, telemetry systems, or other complex control systems.

- Experience integrating security into system design, supplier agreements, procurement, verification, acceptance, and operational readiness.

- Familiarity with relevant cybersecurity, space, export-control, or customer frameworks, including NIST CSF, ISO 27001, IEC 62443, ECSS, or applicable national requirements.

- Relevant certifications or demonstrated experience with security tooling, automation, vulnerability assessment, monitoring, detection, or incident response.

title: Customer Support Team Lead
description:
UpSlide is the document production layer for financial services . We orchestrate LLMs, machine learning, and workflow agents within Microsoft 365 to deliver reliable, quality outputs in the most efficient and cost-effective way. As a Microsoft Solutions Partner, with 14+ years supporting financial services teams, we bring together expertise from the tech, finance, and design fields to help clients like KPMG, BNP Paribas, Rothschild & Co. boost productivity while improving brand consistency across their corporate documents. 

We are a certified B Corporation , upholding the belief that businesses should have a positive impact on society. 

✨ Our values 

Our values guide our approach to work and are at the heart of our recruitment process. To join our team, we look for individuals who value: 

- Excellence: We think that every detail counts, and we place great importance on the quality of our deliverables. 

- Trust: We are passionate, committed, and free to act with autonomy. 

- Happiness at work: We enjoy looking on the bright side and we share our enthusiasm with our colleagues and clients. 

🤝 The team 

You will join our Support team as the direct manager of a group of Support Engineers. While the function operates globally, with part of the team in Paris and the rest in New York, this specific role is based in Paris . 

You will report to Matthieu , Global Head of Scale CS, and your manager, who will support you in achieving your goals. You will also partner closely with Support Operations, Product, Engineering, Professional Services, Customer Success, Sales, and IT. You will also be part of the global Go-To-Market community across our international offices. 

Here is what the Go-To-Market organization looks like at UpSlide: 

- Account Executives: Prospect, acquire new business acquisition and expand existing accounts 

- Consultants: Lead implementation projects, deliver client training, and ensure successful deployment 

- Customer Success Managers: Own a portfolio of accounts end-to-end, driving retention, renewal signing, expansion within existing entities, value realization, and long-term account growth 

- Support Engineers : Resolve day-to-day technical questions and issues, and ensure a smooth customer experience 

🖋️ Your responsibilities 

As Support Team Lead, you will be the direct manager of our Support Engineers and accountable for the team's day-to-day performance, development, and service delivery. You will translate our Support strategy into effective routines, consistent execution, and an excellent customer experience. 

This is a player-coach role . Your primary focus is managing and developing the team, but you'll stay close to operations , supporting complex investigations, reviewing ticket quality, and coordinating escalations when needed. The Head of Support defines the strategy and long-term evolution of the function. You make sure the team delivers on it every day. 

We're looking for someone who is a natural people developer : accountable, structured, thorough, calm under pressure, data-informed, proactive, and collaborative. We strongly believe in growing our people internally, and this role is also a strong stepping stone toward broader Support and Customer Success leadership for those who want to keep growing. 

People Management & Team Development 

Directly manage, coach, and develop the Support Engineers to help them perform at their best and grow in their careers: 

- Hold regular one-to-ones, set clear expectations, and provide frequent, actionable feedback 

- Monitor individual performance, address issues when needed, and lead performance reviews and development plans 

- Identify skills gaps and organize coaching, training, and knowledge-sharing 

- Own onboarding and ramp-up for new team members, and participate in hiring 

- Foster a culture of customer empathy, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement 

Daily Service Delivery & Escalation Management 

Own the daily delivery of Support and act as the first point of management escalation for complex, urgent, or sensitive cases: 

- Monitor ticket queues, backlog, workload, and service levels, and ensure tickets are correctly prioritized and followed through 

- Organize team coverage (absences, shifts, peak periods) and step in when service delivery is at risk 

- Review and coordinate escalated tickets, defining next steps and involving the right internal stakeholders (Product, Engineering, Professional Services, Customer Success) 

- Coordinate customer communication on significant cases, and escalate major risks or executive concerns to the Head of Support 

Quality, Process, & Performance 

Maintain high standards of technical quality, and bring a critical, structured eye to how Support operates today, proposing and driving changes rather than simply preserving the status quo: 

- Identify where tickets could be resolved faster and more efficiently in writing, and reduce the number of cases that unnecessarily escalate into calls, especially multi-stakeholder ones, to protect everyone's time and improve the ROI of customer interactions 

- Review ticket quality using QA tools and scorecards, and coach the team based on the results 

- Ensure investigations are structured, well-documented, and clearly communicated to customers 

- Monitor operational and quality indicators (backlog, response/resolution time, CSAT, quality scores) to identify risks and drive corrective action 

- Document, monitor adoption of, and continuously improve Support workflows, in partnership with Support Operations 

Cross-functional Collaboration 

Make sure Support works effectively with the rest of the business. 

- Coordinate with Product and Engineering on customer investigations and product issues 

- Collaborate with Professional Services, Customer Success, and Sales on customer situations requiring Support involvement, and continuously refine which team owns which type of request across the client lifecycle 

- Clarify responsibilities and handovers between Support and other teams, and represent the team's operational needs in cross-functional discussions 

To work on these tasks, you will mainly use the following tools: Zendesk (or an equivalent ticketing platform), our data stack tools, Microsoft Office, UpSlide, and internal knowledge-base tools (or local equivalents). 

⚡Your goals 

You will be assessed on: 

- Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) 

- Time to Resolution (TTR) 

- Ticket-to-active-user ratio 

- Team engagement and development 

You are a great fit if you have: 

- Proven experience managing or leading a customer-facing team, ideally in B2B SaaS, technical support, or a similar operational environment 

- Strong coaching and people-development skills, including the ability to give clear, constructive, and sometimes difficult feedback 

- Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities across a team 

- Experience using service or operational metrics to identify issues and improve performance 

- Strong customer communication and escalation-management skills 

- Ability to understand technical issues and guide structured investigations, without needing to personally own every ticket 

- Fluent in French & English mandatory 

- Ability to collaborate effectively with Product, Engineering, and other customer-facing teams 

- A pragmatic, accountable approach to problem-solving, with a bias for ownership over escalation 

We’d love it if you have: 

- Experience directly managing a team of five or more people 

- Experience supporting Enterprise customers 

- Experience with Microsoft 365, Office add-ins, deployment, or IT environments 

- Familiarity with Zendesk or a similar ticketing platform 

- Experience with quality and knowledge management, or Support Operations 

- Experience supporting distributed or international teams 

- Familiarity with automation, AI-assisted Support, or self-service strategies 

✨ If you don’t tick all the boxes but you think you’d be a great fit, please apply and tell us why. 

Recruitment process 

- Screening call with a Talent Acquisition Specialist: A conversation to walk through your experience, motivation, and fit for the role. 

- Interview with your future manager or their peer: A deeper dive into your management experience in Support. 

- Case study and a team-meet: A live exercise reflecting real challenges of the role, followed by a conversation with members of the wider team. 

- Final conversation with leadership: A closing discussion to align on ambition, expectations, and next steps. 

🚀 We'll conduct a reference check to learn how to help you thrive. On average, our process lasts 3 weeks.

What we offer 

🌍 International environment: Start-up with five offices (Paris, London, Berlin, New York, Singapore) and users in more than 60 countries 

🌱 Training & professional development: Collaboration with our sister company, IPH , which provides UpSliders with training on key soft skills and management 

🎉 Company events: Office socials and international company events (e.g. annual company seminar, team seminar, and sustainability actions taken throughout the year) 

🏠 Beautiful office: Office near Opéra (1er arrondissement) – a vibrant space with beautiful common areas and meeting rooms, a nap room, bike storage and showers, tea/coffee, etc. 

💻 Hybrid work: 2-3 days in-office per week 

🧑‍💻 Work-from-home budget: €500 WFH equipment budget 

💆‍♀️ Wellness package: 50€ per month for physical and mental wellness activities 

👶 Family support: 

- Paid parental leave for birthing and non-birthing parents 

- 4 days fully paid leave for sick children up to 6 years old or up to €1,800 for childcare reimbursement 

- Flexible return to work options 

- An additional 5 days are fully paid within 6 months after becoming a parent 

✈️ Holidays: 25 vacation days and 9 RTT (with one taken for Solidarity Day) 

✅ General: 

- Meal vouchers (Tickets resto): €11 per day on your Swile card (210 tickets per year) 

- Healthcare insurance (Mutuelle): Covered by Alan. You can extend cover to your partner and children 

- Commute (Transports): Metro, RER, bike, or e-scooter - These options are reimbursed 50% by UpSlide 

As a B Corp-certified company, we have strong commitments toward our employees, community, clients, suppliers, and the environment. We strive to create an environment where everyone feels welcome. This commitment to diversity and inclusion is applied in our recruitment process and your employee experience once you’ve joined UpSlide ✨

title: Senior Key Account Executive
description:
Qui sommes-nous ? 

N2JSoft est une fintech B2B SaaS spécialisée dans la digitalisation des processus RH et financiers, qui développe deux solutions : N2F et Vertical Expense . Tu seras amené(e) à travailler plus particulièrement sur Vertical Expense, notre solution SaaS de gestion des notes de frais qui accompagne les entreprises et les organisations publiques dans leur transformation digitale. 

Notre mission : simplifier, automatiser et sécuriser la gestion des frais professionnels, tout en nous adaptant aux besoins et aux contextes parfois complexes de nos clients. Notre solution est très personnalisable, hautement interopérable, et déployée auprès de structures exigeantes, souvent multi-populations (collaborateurs nomades, agents, intérimaires, prestataires externes…). 

Pour accompagner notre croissance, nous renforçons l'équipe Sales de Vertical Expense . Tu y prendras en charge le développement de grands comptes publics et privés, sur des ventes complexes à forts enjeux. 

Tu auras pour mission de : 

- Piloter le cycle de vente de bout en bout : qualification des opportunités, proposition de valeur différenciante, accès aux décideurs, négociation et closing. 

- Développer de nouvelles opportunités par une prospection ciblée, en complément des leads apportés par le Marketing et par nos équipes Alliances & Channel. 

- Analyser les besoins de tes prospects et présenter la solution, avec l'appui de l'avant-vente sur les projets complexes. 

- Rédiger les réponses aux appels d'offres publics et privés (dont le mémoire technique), en t'appuyant sur les équipes internes. 

- Assurer une passation fluide vers les équipes projets et CSM, et suivre les projets en appui après la signature. 

- Participer aux réflexions stratégiques : veille concurrentielle, tendances du marché, différenciateurs produit. 

Ce qu'on va attendre de toi : 

- Tu as une expérience significative et récente en vente complexe SaaS B2B auprès de grands comptes. 

- Tu as déjà mené des cycles de vente longs, dans des organisations multi-décideurs, en travaillant avec des partenaires et des influenceurs. 

- Tu as un vrai goût pour la chasse : aller chercher de nouveaux clients te motive. 

- Tu es à l'aise face à des interlocuteurs C-level et tu sais adapter ton discours à chacun (idéalement DAF, DRH, Travel Manager, DSI…). 

- Tu sais répondre à un appel d'offres avec rigueur, de la réponse au mémoire technique. 

- Tu comprends les solutions SaaS, web et mobiles. 

- Tu es autonome, organisé(e) et tenace, et tu sais rebondir face à un deal perdu. 

- Tu aimes travailler en équipe avec le Marketing, l’équipe Alliance/Channel, les équipes projets et le Produit. 

- Tu es à l'aise avec des déplacements réguliers chez les clients (environ une fois par semaine). 

C'est un plus si : 

- Tu connais l'univers des notes de frais ou du voyage d'affaires. 

- Tu parles anglais. 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 

- Un poste stratégique, au cœur de notre développement sur les grands comptes publics et privés. 

- Pas que de la prospection à froid : une partie des leads vient du Marketing et de nos partenaires. 

- Une vision complète du cycle de vente, jusqu'au suivi du projet client. 

- Une équipe stable, fière de ses grands comptes, avec le sens du service et de l'excellence. 

- Une ambiance où l'on ne se prend pas au sérieux : team building réguliers… 

Processus de recrutement : 

- Entretien téléphonique RH. 

- Entretien avec le manager. 

- Mise en situation : étude de cas sur un compte client fictif. 

- Entretien final avec la Direction. 

Localisation : Montagnat (01) et Aix-en-Provence, avec 1 jour par semaine sur chaque site et 3 jours de télétravail. 

Rémunération : fixe : 60K € - 80K€ + variable

- Développer les principes d'identité visuelle destinés au Retail Design, aux expériences de marque et aux activations.

- Participer au développement de nouveaux formats digitaux, motion et contenus innovants.

- Encadrer la déclinaison graphique des identités sur les différents supports.

description:
Product Marketing Director 

Reports to: Chief Commercial Officer 

Location: UK, France, Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Austria, Spain, Finland, USA. Some travel to our offices will be required from time-to-time

You must have the right to work in one the above countries in order to be considered for the role.

💼 About the role 

PQShield is looking for a Product Marketing Director who can turn complex technology into stories that people understand, remember, and act on.

You will own how PQShield's products, technology, and vision are positioned, communicated, and brought to market worldwide. You'll sit at the intersection of product, engineering, sales, customers, and the broader security market — translating breakthrough cryptography and security technology into compelling narratives for executives, engineers, partners, and buyers.

This role is for a strategic product marketer and exceptional storyteller who can identify the market shift, understand the customer problem, and turn complex technology into differentiated positioning that creates urgency, preference and demand. 

Since NIST published its first post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards, which the PQShield team co-authored, organizations across semiconductors, automotive, defense, and enterprise face significant challenges in preparing for the post-quantum transition. This role will help define the market narrative around that transition, position PQShield's portfolio within it and give customers a clear reason to act.

⚒️ What you’ll be doing 

- Own the story: Develop the narrative, positioning, messaging, and value propositions that explain what is changing in the market, why customers need to act, the problem PQShield solves, and why our approach is differentiated.

- Turn technical capability into customer value: Work with cryptographers, engineers and product leaders to understand sophisticated technology, identify what matters to the buyer and translate technical capabilities into clear business and security value without sacrificing technical credibility.

- Position the portfolio: Own positioning and messaging for our hardware IP and software portfolio, including PQPlatform, PQPerform, PQCryptoLib, and PQMicroLib. Build a clear messaging architecture that connects the portfolio while preserving the differentiated value of each offering.

- Understand the customer: Develop deep insight into customer problems, buying journeys, security requirements, regulatory pressures, barriers to adoption, buying dynamics, and the forces driving post-quantum adoption. Turn those insights into sharper products, messaging, and go-to-market strategies.

- Shape category and market narrative: Help define how PQShield talks about post-quantum security, cryptographic agility, and the transition to quantum-safe systems — and how we differentiate our approach in a rapidly evolving market.

- Lead product launches: Create and execute compelling go-to-market strategies for new products, certifications, partnerships, and major releases.

- Equip the sales team: Build compelling presentations, stories, solution briefs, case studies, battlecards, and other tools that help sales teams communicate value and win complex deals.

- Build buyer and segment-specific stories: Develop differentiated narratives for semiconductors, automotive, military and aerospace, industrial IoT, networking, and enterprise, adapting the value story for different buyers, use cases and business priorities.

- Own competitive storytelling: Understand the competitive landscape and turn technical and commercial differences into clear, credible differentiation.

- Create exceptional content: Lead the development of white papers, thought leadership, application notes, customer stories, executive content, web experiences, and other material that establishes PQShield as a category leader.

- Bring customer stories to life: Find and develop the stories that demonstrate why customers are making the transition to post-quantum security and why they choose PQShield.

- Work across the company: Partner closely with product, engineering, sales, partnerships, and leadership to ensure the market sees one clear, compelling PQShield story.

🎯 Required Skills And Qualifications 

We're looking for an experienced product marketing leader who is exceptionally strong in positioning, messaging and strategic storytelling. You can take an emerging market, complicated buyer problem or deeply technical product and find the clear narrative inside it.

- 8+ years of marketing experience, with significant experience in product marketing, technology marketing, B2B marketing, or a closely related discipline.

- A proven ability to develop positioning and stories that change how markets understand a product, technology, or company.

- Exceptional written and verbal communication skills. You can take something highly technical and make it understandable, interesting, and compelling without dumbing it down.

- Strong storytelling instincts and the ability to find the human, business, and strategic narrative inside complex technology.

- Experience marketing technical B2B products, ideally in cybersecurity, semiconductors, infrastructure, embedded systems, software, or another sophisticated technology market.

- Strong understanding of security and technology buyers, and the ability to communicate credibly with CISOs, CTOs, engineers, architects, product leaders, and business executives.

- Demonstrated ability to work closely with technical experts and quickly develop enough subject-matter expertise to challenge assumptions, ask good questions, and tell an accurate story.

- A strong commercial mindset: you understand that great marketing isn't just about explaining a product — it's about creating differentiation, urgency, preference, and ultimately revenue.

- Experience launching products and taking complex offerings to market.

- Experience developing compelling sales narratives and enablement for complex, multi-stakeholder sales.

- Excellent strategic judgment, with the ability to determine what the market needs to hear, why it matters, and how PQShield should say it.

- Comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where you will often need to create the narrative before the market has established one.

What we can offer you 

- A competitive compensation package.

- Share options.

- A remote first company. You will work from home most of the time, but will need to join us in the office for planning sessions and key meetings as required.

- Travel for customer meetings and marketing events as needed. 

- Health insurance.

- Generous PTO and holiday package.

- Company contributions towards 401K/pension

- …and other great benefits.

If you enjoy working as part of a technology company, value the security of our daily digital lives, and love solving hard problems - then we’d love to hear from you.

title: Backend Engineer - Mission Operations Services
description:
Loft Orbital is looking for a Backend Engineer to join our Mission Operations Services (MOS) team. MOS owns the backend services that let Loft operators and customers command, monitor, and automate our satellite fleet through Cockpit, our mission control system. You’ll help build and scale the microservices that sit between ground and flight software, turning high-level intent into safe, reliable on-orbit operations.

You’ll work across multiple satellite platforms and collaborate closely with backend, flight software, embedded systems, test, and satellite operations teams. This is a hands-on engineering role where you’ll both build new systems and help debug live missions. We also offer SatDevOps training, so you don’t just write the tools - you actually use them to operate spacecraft.

If you’re excited about building backend systems that directly control satellites - and you like the idea of both shipping code and helping fly missions - we’d love to hear from you.

About this Role 

- Design and build backend tools for operations : services that power passes, autopilots, activities, and day‑to‑day satellite operations.

- Handle commands and telemetry across multiple satellite buses and ground segment providers, with a strong focus on safety, robustness, and observability.

- Write production backend code in Python, owning services end‑to‑end from design and implementation through deployment and maintenance.

- Collaborate with flight software, embedded software, integration and test, and space infrastructure teams to integrate new satellite buses and capabilities into Cockpit.

- Support internal users of Cockpit (operators, test engineers, solutions engineers) by improving APIs, workflows, and debugging tools.

- Have the opportunity to take part in spacecraft operations through SatDevOps rotations, occasionally helping investigate anomalies and supporting real‑time incident response when needed.

Must Haves: 

- 4+ years of relevant backend software engineering experience in production environments

- Solid Python development experience in a production environment.

- Experience with Docker and container‑based development.

- Hands‑on experience with backend web development frameworks (e.g., Django, Flask, FastAPI, etc.).

- Proven API design skills (designing, documenting, and maintaining HTTP/GraphQL/REST‑style APIs).

Nice to Haves: 

- Experience with Django and/or GraphQL.

- Strong database fundamentals and practical experience (e.g., Postgres, time‑series DBs).

- Exposure to Kubernetes in production.

- Familiarity with InfluxDB / TimescaleDB or other time‑series systems.

- Background in mission‑critical, distributed, or real‑time systems (space or otherwise).

Some of Our Awesome Benefits: 

- Equity, we want you to have an active role in our success

- Up to 35 days of Paid Time Off (vacations & RTT ) and flexible working hours, we want you to be at your best

- Health and life insurance, we care about your health

- Lunch Vouchers, because let’s be honest, we love food! (we even have a slack channel about it #loft-gourmand )

- Cross-office travel opportunities between San Francisco, Colorado, and Toulouse to learn from our differences

- Company and team off-sites and many other events to work & celebrate together

- Relocation assistance to Toulouse when applicable

Who We Are: Founded in 2017, Loft provides governments, companies, and research institutions with a fast, reliable, and simple way to deploy missions in orbit.

We integrate, launch, and operate spacecraft, offering end-to-end missions as a service across Earth observation, IoT connectivity, on-orbit AI, national security missions, and more. Leveraging our existing space infrastructure and an extensive inventory of satellite buses, Loft is reducing years-long integration and launch timelines to months. title: Global Head of AI Deployment & Partner Delivery
description:
About Dust 

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. 

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. 

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 .

Summary 

Dust is hiring a Head of AI Deployment & Partner Delivery to make high-impact Dust deployments repeatable at scale.

When customers deploy Dust well, AI agents become part of how their teams work every day. Your job is to make that happen consistently, whether a deployment is led by Dust or by a trusted partner. You will lead our most complex customer deployments, turn what works, technically and organizationally, into clear playbooks, and build the partner delivery capacity that lets more customers succeed with Dust in 2027 and beyond.

This is a player-coach leadership role. You will lead and grow Dust’s global AI Deployment team, stay directly involved in our most important deployments, and build the methods, standards, and partner network that allow delivery to scale without depending on you for every engagement.

You will work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering to connect what customers want to achieve with how deployments are planned, delivered, and measured.

This is a chance to define how an AI-native company delivers transformation: what an exceptional deployment looks like, how value is measured, and how partners become delivery teams our customers trust.

What you’ll do 

Lead and grow the global AI Deployment team 

- Lead Dust’s existing global AI Deployment team and set its direction, priorities, and standards.

- Hire and develop deployment leaders and practitioners as customer demand grows.

- Shape roles, career paths, and coverage across regions, customer segments, and deployment types.

- Coach the team through complex customer situations and hold a consistently high bar for the work.

- Set up the operating rhythms, capacity planning, and reporting the function needs to scale.

Define how Dust deployments are delivered 

- Build one deployment method, from discovery through handoff, that Dust and partner teams can both follow to the same standard.

- Define which deployments Dust should lead, which a partner can deliver well, and how work moves between the two.

- Set clear entry and exit criteria and go-live readiness checks, and track delivery health: time to first value, go-live quality, and customer satisfaction.

- Run regular delivery reviews, spot at-risk engagements early, and bring the right Dust and partner people together quickly when a deployment is blocked.

- Turn lessons from each engagement into reusable playbooks, templates, and reference architectures, and recurring friction into clear input for Product and Engineering.

Lead AI transformation with strategic customers 

- Personally lead complex, high-priority, and first-of-their-kind deployments, from scoping to lasting adoption, bringing in Solutions Engineering, Product, and Engineering when complexity or risk calls for it.

- Help customer leaders define what AI transformation means for their organization: map how teams work today and identify the workflows where agents can create the most value.

- Align executives, IT, security, and business teams on goals, use cases, and success measures, with a baseline before launch and measured impact after.

- Design change programs for each deployment: executive sponsorship, communication plans, role-based enablement, and clear adoption milestones.

- Develop AI operators and champions inside customer teams, and help customers update ways of working, governance, and ownership so agents become part of how teams operate.

- Track adoption after launch, act quickly when teams aren’t changing how they work, and hand off to Customer Success with a clear picture of what comes next.

Build a high-quality partner delivery network 

- Work with Partnerships to assess partners’ delivery capability, technical depth, and customer readiness.

- Start with a small, carefully selected group of partner practitioners and grow capacity as quality is proven.

- Co-create onboarding, training, certification, and train-the-trainer programs so partners can develop their own Dust experts.

- Co-deliver early partner engagements, then help partners progress toward delivering independently, leading adoption, not just implementation.

- Ensure customers experience Dust and its partners as one aligned team, with clear responsibilities on every engagement.

Requirements 

- You have at least 6 years of experience leading and developing customer-facing deployment or delivery teams, ideally across multiple regions or customer segments and through periods of fast change.

- You have led complex enterprise deployments or transformation programs and delivered measurable customer outcomes.

- You have built or significantly improved a deployment methodology, professional services model, or delivery function, adding the structure needed to scale without unnecessary process.

- You have led organizational change alongside technology rollouts, and built champion networks or adoption plans that changed how teams work after the project ended.

You don’t need to be a machine-learning engineer. Beyond that, we care more about evidence that you have built high-performing delivery systems than about a perfect sequence of titles.

- You understand how systems integrators, consultancies, and implementation partners staff, deliver, and grow a practice, and you have built enablement or certification programs that created lasting capability in teams you didn’t manage.

- You have turned around engagements at risk from scope, staffing, technical complexity, or stakeholder misalignment, and you know when to standardize, when to adapt, and when to reset.

- You are credible with customer executives, partner leaders, and technical practitioners, and you communicate clearly with all of them.

- You are a hands-on, low-ego leader with a builder’s instinct: you would rather solve the problem than hand off a recommendation.

- You are comfortable traveling to customers and partners when it matters most.

AI and technical credibility 

- Advise customers on where AI agents can create meaningful value and where they can’t yet, and explain why to technical teams, business leaders, and executives.

- Understand how agents work in practice: prompting, context, tool use, retrieval, evaluations, reliability, and cost.

- Challenge a deployment plan’s assumptions about integrations, data connectors, authentication, permissions, security, and production readiness, and discuss the trade-offs with engineers.

- Design evaluation approaches that connect AI performance to customer and business outcomes.

Location 

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust 

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. 

Learn how we think and work.

title: Head of Hardware
description:
Accelerating embodied AGI. 

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Head of Hardware, you own that hardware end to end: electrical, firmware, and the mechanical integration that holds it together, from the first schematic to devices running on factory floors.

You lead the team that builds it. Today that is about six engineers on robotics, three on EMG sensing, and three on camera systems, plus contractors, and it will grow quickly. Our Electrical Engineer and Embedded Engineer roles report to you. You set the architecture they build against, and you still build alongside them.

This is a founder-shaped role, not a management seat. We are looking for someone who has carried a product from a blank page to customers with real skin in the game, wants to build both the thing and the team that builds it, and would rather design than review. If that sounds like you, you will want to do it again at the earliest stage.

What You Will Do

- Own the hardware roadmap for Shift and Atlas data capture: wearables, sensor rigs, camera systems, and prototype robots. What we build, in what order, and why.

- Set the system architecture across electrical, firmware, and mechanical: sensors, compute, power, wireless, and enclosures. Make the trade-offs, and make them stick when disciplines disagree.

- Stay on the bench: schematics, layout reviews, board bring-up, and a scope in your hands when the team is stuck. On the days it matters, you are the best electrical engineer in the room.

- Lead and grow the team: hire, set the bar, run design reviews, and give engineers ownership of whole subsystems rather than tickets.

- Guarantee data quality end to end: EMG and EEG front ends, camera pipelines, IMUs, and synchronization across many devices, so that what reaches the ML team is clean, time-aligned, and trustworthy.

- Take designs from prototype to small-batch production: DFM, component and EMS vendors, test fixtures, certification, and field reliability.

- Work shoulder to shoulder with ML and deployment. Your hardware decides what the training data looks like, and you will be on the floor where it is captured.

- Run contractors and partners without losing ownership of the result.

Requirements

- You have taken at least one product from zero to shipped, with significant ownership of the outcome: as a co-founder, CTO, first hardware hire, or the lead who owned the whole device. Not one subsystem, not one phase. Ideally a wearable, at a tier-one hardware company known for shipping at scale.

- Electrical engineering is your home discipline. You have designed boards that shipped, across mixed-signal, power, wireless, and high-speed digital, and you can still do it today.

- You think in systems. You understand how an electrode choice, an enclosure tolerance, and an ADC sample rate interact, and you can hold the mechanical and firmware conversations as a peer, not a customer.

- You have led engineers: hired them, grown them, and kept a team shipping through 0-to-1 ambiguity. Typically 6+ years in hardware, but we care more about what you shipped than how long it took.

- A strong understanding of how hardware decisions affect data quality. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you design accordingly.

- Experience taking hardware to small-batch production: DFM, vendor and EMS management, test, and certification.

- Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice.

- High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. A 0-to-1 hardware program takes the hours it takes, in person and at pace, and you have chosen that before.

- Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care.

Nice to Have

- Wearables, smartwatches, drones, robotics, AR/VR, or defense wearables on your résumé.

- Camera systems: sensor selection, MIPI and ISP pipelines, and multi-camera synchronization.

- Low-power and battery design, BLE or Wi-Fi, and antenna integration in small enclosures.

- Enough mechanical fluency (CAD, tolerances, and materials) to challenge the mechanical team’s choices and be right some of the time.

- Prior founder or founding-engineer experience, including the parts that went wrong.

- Open-source hardware or firmware contributions.

Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

- Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

- Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

- Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

- Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if: 

- You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

- You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

- You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if: 

- You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

- You would forward output you cannot explain.

- "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

- Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

- Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

- Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

- Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

- Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

- Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

- Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

- A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

- Free food and drinks in the office.

Equal Opportunity

MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.

Swissblock is a private investment firm dedicated to cross-asset investing. We employ a systematic framework that integrates robust algorithmic trading with exhaustive market analysis. title: Founder Associate to the CTO
description:
The Role 
As Founders Associate in our office in Zurich, you'll be the right hand of our CTO, Max. You run the daily business of the CTO office, own strategic projects from start to finish, drive the first round of our technical hiring, and bridge technology and business. This is a true zero-to-one mandate.
Whether you come from computer science or business, you combine strong tech understanding with real commercial thinking. You won't be writing production code, but you'll understand our product and infrastructure well, be a trusted counterpart for our engineers, and know what technical decisions mean for the business.

What You'll Do 

- CTO Office & Executive Support 

- Manage our CTO's priorities so his time goes to what matters most

- Prepare briefing documents and agendas for important meetings and make sure every action item gets followed up

- Technical Hiring 

- Run first-round calls with engineering candidates and coordinate the interview process with our team

- Strategic Projects 

- Take full ownership of critical projects, from deep dives into emerging tech trends to board-level material

- Evaluate and drive strategic technical partnerships that keep us at the forefront of AI infrastructure

- Tech x Business 

- Translate technical topics into commercial decisions and clear stories for customers, partners and investors

- Support pricing, product and go-to-market questions with a technical angle

- Build the processes the CTO office and engineering team need to scale

What We're Looking For 

- Studies (preferably Master level) or a degree in computer science or a related technical field, OR in business, economics or management with a strong understanding of technology

- Very good commercial understanding: you think in business impact, not just technology

- Real curiosity for tech: you can follow and discuss AI and infrastructure topics with engineers

- First practical experience in a fast-paced environment such as a startup, consulting or VC

- Builder's mindset: you take high ownership and enjoy building processes from scratch

- Hustle & execution: you're pragmatic and move fast without losing sight of quality – a "get shit done" mentality is essential

- Organizational talent: you stay calm under pressure and work in a highly structured and precise way

description:
This is Cradle

Proteins are the molecular machines of life, used for many therapeutic, diagnostic, chemical, agricultural and food applications. Designing and optimizing proteins takes a lot of expert knowledge and manual effort, through the use of custom computational and biological tools. 

Machine learning is revolutionizing this space, by enabling high-fidelity protein models. At Cradle, we offer a software platform for AI-guided discovery and optimization of proteins, so that biologists can design proteins faster and at scale. We are already used by clients across biopharma, biotech, agri-tech, food-tech, and academia.

We're an experienced team of just under 100 people. We've built many successful products before and have enough funding for multiple years of runway. We are distributed across three offices in Amsterdam, Boston, and Zurich, alongside a few remote colleagues.

We offer our employees a very competitive salary, a generous equity stake in the company and a wide range of benefits and career progression opportunities.

The Role 

As Executive Assistant at Cradle, you'll keep two of our founding executives moving. Between customer visits, investor meetings, hiring and travel across Amsterdam, Zurich and the US, there's a lot to keep track of, and your job is to make sure nothing gets dropped. You'll own their calendars, inboxes and travel, and take care of the personal admin that would otherwise eat into their time. This role suits someone who likes being trusted with the whole picture, professional and personal, and treats both with the same care.

Responsibilities 

- Run two calendars as one system: Protect focus time, balance competing priorities across time zones, and decide what deserves a meeting and what can be an email.

- Own the inbox front line: Triage, draft and reply on their behalf to customers, investors, candidates and the team, so the important things surface and the rest gets handled.

- Plan travel end to end: Customer visits, conferences and trips between Amsterdam, Zurich and the US, from flights and hotels to the meeting room and dinner booking on the other side.

- Take care of personal and life admin: Appointments, household logistics, official paperwork, bills and renewals, handled so none of it lands on their desks.

- Prepare every important meeting: Make sure briefs and context are ready beforehand, and follow up on decisions and action items afterwards.

- Make recurring admin disappear: Automate repeated processes so they mostly run themselves.

Requirements 

The best people we've hired didn't match a checklist. Below is a list of what matters most for this role. If you bring most of it and are curious about the rest, we'd love to hear from you: 

- 4+ years supporting senior executives, ideally more than one at a time

- Sharp judgment about what's urgent, what can wait and what never needs to reach the exec

- Clear, polished written English

- You spot the next problem before anyone asks and fix it

- Experience handling personal admin alongside the professional side, with the discretion that comes with it

- Organised and dependable without needing a rigid structure; at a ~90-person company you'll often build the process yourself

- At home in Google Workspace and quick to pick up new software tools

Nice to Haves 

These aren't requirements, but they'd give you a head start:

- German fluency would be idea to would make local appointments, paperwork and authorities much easier

- Experience in a startup or scale-up environment

- Familiarity with Swiss administrative procedures (permits, insurance, tax paperwork, relocations)

- Experience with task tools like Todoist, Notion or Linear

Our commitment to inclusive hiring

Cradle evaluates all candidates based on merit, regardless of sex, gender, ethnicity, socio-economic background, or any other aspect of identity. We maintain zero tolerance for discrimination and actively encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

AI disclosure

Cradle uses an applicant tracking system that includes basic AI-assisted features which may generate scores or rankings based on how applications match a job description. These outputs are not used to make or meaningfully influence hiring decisions — all candidates are evaluated through a thorough, human-led review by our recruiting team.

Please be aware that scammers are posing as us in order to get your personal details or money.
